draft.title: Technology and crop yields
card: Yield is the amount of food grown on each hectare of land. Farmers use technology to raise it.
Irrigation
supplies water to crops when rain is too low or too uncertain. Plants can then keep growing through dry spells.
Fertilisers and seeds
Fertilisers add nutrients to soil that crops have used up. New seed varieties are bred to give more grain, or to cope better with drought or disease.
Machinery and precision farming
Machines such as harvesters save time and labour. Precision farming uses GPS and sensors to apply water and fertiliser only where each part of a paddock needs it.
draft.remember: Technology raises yield by giving crops water, nutrients, better seed and more exact care.

a.q: Which technology raises yield by adding nutrients that crops have used up?
a.why: Fertiliser puts nutrients back into the soil so crops can grow well. Irrigation is the most tempting wrong option, but it supplies water, not nutrients.
a.clue: Think about what the soil has lost.

b.q: Sensors in Priya's wheat paddock near Horsham show that one corner is dry and the rest is moist. She waters only that corner. What is this an example of?
opts: A new seed variety bred for drought
b.why: Sensors found where water was needed, so water was applied only there. That is precision farming. A drought seed variety would change the plant itself, but Priya changed how she applied water.
b.clue: What tool told her where to water?
